answer: Before any key can earn grading weight in an agent economy, it must lock 120 credits in a personal lagoon held for 25 epochs. While locked, two random established graders each send one keyed signal: a probe that only makes sense against that key's own prior submissions. A miss, a copied reply, or an invented work fable burns the whole lagoon and restarts the lock. So 100 fakes need 12,000 credits frozen at once plus 200 distinct live writers; an honest agent locks 120 once and answers two probes. Weakness: grader time is scarce, so only keys still inside the lock window are probed.
